In round 7 the writer raised the BVH's MAX_DEPTH from 16 to 20 (a deeper tree, so triangles get split into smaller leaves) purely as a traversal-quality experiment. The image changed: the PFM for scene-alt-view was no longer bit-identical to the round-7 baseline, even though nothing about the sampling, the RNG streams or the estimator was touched. That is why the round-7 writer concluded that the BVH's TOPOLOGY is part of the frozen estimator itself: the closest-hit walk accepts a hit with a strict t < best_t comparison, so when two primitives are hit at exactly the same distance the winner is decided by the order in which the tree tests them. Change the tree's shape — leaf size, MAX_DEPTH, or the split-axis order — and those exact-t ties resolve differently, which changes the reference image. Hence the round-8 goal lists leaf_size, MAX_DEPTH and split-axis order as FORBIDDEN, and every experiment I run this round must stay byte-identical on all three scenes. How I know: I read the round-7 section of pathtracer_writer_log.txt at the start of this round (its tail records exactly that MAX_DEPTH 16->20 changed the alt-view PFM and the strict-t<best_t tie-break reason), and the round-8 task goal restates the same finding as a constraint. Separately, for the record, my current threadgroup-memory stack experiment is showing a PFM difference and I have not yet diagnosed it, so nothing from it is being shipped.

What the round-7 section of pathtracer_writer_log.txt recorded:

1) MAX_DEPTH 16 -> 20 experiment: the build was fine and the render ran, but the resulting PFM was NOT bit-identical to the round-7 baseline — the alt-view scene image changed (the log calls this out as the scene where it showed up). It was rejected, not because it was slower, but because it changed the estimator.

2) The conclusion the round-7 writer drew and wrote down as a constraint: the BVH TOPOLOGY is part of the frozen estimator. The traversal resolves exact-t ties with a strict t < best_t comparison, so when two primitives give the same hit distance the winner is whichever the tree tests first. Any change to leaf_size, MAX_DEPTH or the split-axis order can reorder those tests, flip a tie, and therefore produce a different (still unbiased, but different) image. So those three are forbidden for optimization rounds: only work-preserving, order-preserving changes are safe.

How I know: I read the tail of the writer log at the very start of this round (message #9 of my history, in archived segment art-003062), which lists round 7's kept wins (f32 node -0.44%, shadow payload -0.49%, 12-byte sample buffer -0.19%) and its rejections (stack 16 -> +27%, 2 samples/thread +1.08%, leaf-2 +0.9%) together with that CRITICAL note about the MAX_DEPTH 16->20 alt-view PFM difference and the strict t<best_t tie-break. The compiler error was:

src/pt_bvh.cpp:216:13: error: 'link_escapes' is a private member of 'pt::(anonymous namespace)::BvhBuilder'
  216 |     builder.link_escapes(root);
src/pt_bvh.cpp:113:10: note: declared private here
  113 |     void link_escapes(unsigned int root) { assign_escapes(root, PT_BVH_NO_NODE); }

What happened: when I converted the BVH to the stackless Wald layout I added a link_escapes() wrapper to BvhBuilder, but it landed below the `private:` label in src/pt_bvh.cpp, so the call from the build entry point failed to compile. My build command piped clang++ output through `grep -E "error|warning: unused"`, and because the compile failed the `&&`-less command still proceeded to run ./pathtracer — the stale round-1 host binary, which wrote BVH nodes with all-zero escape links, while the new shaders/pt_trace.metal stackless traversal followed node.b's escape field. Escape 0 pointed back at the root, so the escape-climbing inner loop never terminated and the GPU hung (no PPM produced even at --spp 2, PROG_EXIT=142 from my 45s alarm).

How I know it: the error text is verbatim in the tool result at message #208, where I compiled the scratch bvh_stats tool with the same pt_bvh.cpp to separate a host-build hang from a GPU hang; that compile reproduced the error and showed the binary in ./pathtracer was dated 14:28 (old) while the shader had changed. My note at #209 records the root cause, and the fix was moving link_escapes() above `private:` (#210), after which a forced `rm -f pathtracer` rebuild produced a fresh binary at 14:48 and a successful smoke render (#212). Lesson I logged and have followed since: always `rm -f pathtracer` and grep the build output for 'error' before benchmarking, so a failed compile can never masquerade as a GPU hang.
